reason: Moldova shows the same mechanism as North Macedonia (MEC-11), with the only portfolio-wide service-level use data in the three cases, though these date from 2022. The Commission still named low demand in 2025, the same report that says access and use 'significantly increased', and the agency's 71% of requests online in 2026 is unverified, so the later reported rise qualifies the match without removing it. The context differs: EVO is described as a modular front end over the portal with a recent, untested single-portal claim, a long donor project and a dedicated agency.

Albania matches on one portal, depth of transactions, inclusion and coordination (MEC-08), but it differs on the core symptom because reported use is high, not low. It is a contrast case for consolidation and for range as the Commission reports it, although the RCC says Albania lags the regional average on service scope and sophistication (50 against 53), and it cannot explain what produces use.

Montenegro is the closest match in problem: a live portal, too few transactional services, low use, services run outside the portal and capacity limits (MEC-03, MEC-11). The match is on the problem and not on a solution, because the results are too early and unverified and its portal is newer than North Macedonia's.

The source states that launch does not bring use, which matches North Macedonia's record of 292,179 users with 2,070 monthly applications. It transfers on condition that North Macedonia's low use has the same character, services available but unused, which its figures suggest but do not show service by service; it does not say what would raise use.

The item states a lesson: building without beneficiaries' opinions harms use, which the brief asserts without a test. It applies on condition that user involvement is part of design and that the services people want exist. North Macedonia's Reform Agenda prioritises usability, but the cited item says nothing about consulting beneficiaries, so the first condition is unmet at present.

The item states a general lesson drawn from Montenegro's record, that digitalisation is a matter of political will and institutional capacity. The transfer holds for capacity only, on condition that North Macedonia's unfilled posts and fragmented ownership are tackled along with the technology; the cited items do not support political will, which is insufficient_evidence. The event report is rated Low and gives no proof; item 0016 assigns the same sentence to a ministry official, but the source shows the report's closing line, to correct at the gate.
